newsitem.title: USA: Hedge funds do well on currencies in October -- TASS.
newsitem.headline: Hedge funds do well on currencies in October -- TASS.

text.p: Hedge funds and commodity funds registered some of their biggest gains this year in October, research company TASS Management Ltd said Thursday.
Many of the top 10 programs monitored by TASS registered returns of nearly 20 percent for the month.

Some of the best performing commodity trading advisors (CTA) programs were trend followers who earned high returns from strategies tied to global currency and interest rate markets, TASS chief executive Nicola Meaden said.
The dollar rallied to a 42-month high last week against yen and the mark/yen rate broke out to the upside from a three-month range.
Strategies involving the British pound and Japanese yen in particular were contributors to the solid performance of many trading programs, Meaden said.

"But what seems to have worked well for many managers this year and last month is the European convergence trade," she said. "In this trade, managers bet that the difference in interest rates among European countries will narrow as the region moves to a single currency."

An example of a convergence trade has been buying Italian bonds with the expectation that Italian interest rates will decline while selling German bonds in anticipation of higher German interest rates, Meaden said.
October and April 1996 rank as the two best months this yearfor the commodity trading programs measured by the TASS report.
The TASS monthly report follows the performance of 68 commodity trading advisory programs, each with a minimum of $45 million under management.
TASS Management Inc is a London-based research company which tracks the performance of about 1,600 "alternative investment" managers and funds globally with a total of $9 billion under management.
"Alternative investments" include hedge funds, CTA programs, managed currency managers, emerging market funds and funds of funds.
